researchSummary: My research programme centers on valorizing plant, fruit and food-processing waste into functional biopolymers, nanomucilages and carbon quantum dots for food applications. I develop edible coatings and nanoemulsions from fruit mucilage and seed oils to extend the shelf life of fresh-cut produce, and I engineer plant protein concentrates (chickpea, pea, kidney bean) through modification techniques like succinylation, ultrasonication and fermentation to improve functional and nutritional properties. I also work on carbon quantum dots for fluorescence-based detection of plasticizers and contaminants, photocatalytic dye degradation, biodegradable packaging films, and fat replacers for healthier food product formulation.

researchSummary: My research programme is in laser-plasma physics, focusing on laser wakefield acceleration and terahertz radiation generation. I model electron energy gain using various shaped laser pulses, including Gaussian, Hermite-Gaussian, sinh and cosh Gaussian, and chirped pulses, in homogeneous and magnetized plasmas, and I study terahertz and harmonic generation via nonlinear laser-plasma and laser-carbon-nanotube interactions under static and wiggler magnetic fields. My work is largely analytical and computational, optimizing pulse and plasma parameters for electron acceleration efficiency.

researchSummary: I work theoretically on the propagation of structured laser beams (q-Gaussian, Cosh-Gaussian, Laguerre-Gaussian, Bessel-Gauss and quadruple-Gaussian profiles) through nonlinear and plasma media, focusing on self-focusing, self-trapping, self-phase modulation and self-channeling effects. My studies model electron plasma wave excitation, electron acceleration, ion acoustic wave generation, stimulated Raman scattering and higher harmonic generation in axially and radially inhomogeneous, collisional and collisionless plasmas. I also examine breather optical soliton formation and diffraction management in cubic-quintic nonlinear Kerr media, including applications relevant to slow light and quantum computing.

researchSummary: I work in two connected areas of applied mathematics. In pure analysis, I establish fixed point and coincidence point theorems in generalized metric spaces, especially C*-algebra valued and multiplicative m-metric spaces, with applications to integral equations. In computational fluid mechanics, I use radial basis function pseudospectral methods, homotopy perturbation, and related semi-analytical techniques to study unsteady MHD flow of nanofluids, dusty fluids, and Casson micropolar fluids in channels and ducts, including heat transfer and fuzzy pressure-gradient effects. I also apply fuzzy and neutrosophic programming to optimization problems.

I use molecular docking, pharmacophore mapping, and virtual screening to design and predict activity of glucokinase activators, indole and azole derivatives, and heterocyclic antidiabetic agents, along with ADMET and toxicokinetic prediction of novel leads. I also study chalcone derivatives with dual COX-2/5-LOX inhibitory activity as anti-inflammatory agents, and examine polyphenols and antifungal dienones, integrating in silico prediction with pharmacological rationale for lead compound development.

publications.title: Tailoring Ni-Mg spinel ferrites with gallium doping for enhanced supercapacitor applications
